overview: This table defines each shikigami summon, including its behavior, health, cooldowns, movement, appearance, sounds, and voice lines.
description: Core shikigami (summon) definition: row ID and actor Blueprint, linked action/animation/material/effect/sound/voice/unique rows, action and bone controller selection, HP/down gauges, summon/order cooldowns, instance-death and immortality flags, and auto-attack ranges.

ID.simple: The summon's unique name. The game uses it to connect this shikigami to characters, scenes, and battle displays.
ID.technical: FName row key; all 20 exported row keys equal Id. Battle preload/spawn/sequencer join CharacterShikigami.Id_Shikigami[] to ShikigamiDataTables (+0x6C0), while capture uses CharacterCaptureRow.Id_ShikigamiCharacter. The manager's table arrays are searched in registration order and return the first matching row (the current build registers one ShikigamiDataTable), and these callers skip a missing row. The cached AGameShikigami::ShikigamiRow->Id is also used by sequencer binding lookup and character-specific battle UI. Exported rows are CN_010 through CN_280, including the CN_050/051/052 variants.

FileName_BP.simple: The name of the summon the game loads and places into battle. Changing it swaps which summon appears.
FileName_BP.technical: FName primary-asset loader key derived from the row ID: base rows use <ID>_00_BP (e.g. CN_010_00_BP) and the three _10 variants use <ID>_BP (e.g. CN_050_10_BP). Battle preload creates Shikigami primary-asset loaders from it and appends it to the shikigami asset list; battle spawn and level-sequencer spawn use the loaded class from StudioShikigamiLoaders_950. Capture setup calls Slot.ShikigamiLoaders.FindChecked on it, so an unregistered key is fatal there. Used with GamePrimaryAssetType_Shikigami.

Id_ShikigamiMaterial.simple: Which surface pattern appears on this summon when its look changes. Leaving it empty keeps the current appearance.
Id_ShikigamiMaterial.technical: FName; None in 16/20 exports, otherwise CN_040, CN_052 (two rows) or CN_080. Resolved on demand by UGameShikigamiMaterialController when a pattern is applied, via ShikigamiMaterialDataTables (+0x6D0): SetMaterialPattern(0, nullptr) at spawn and later SetMaterialPattern/AddMaterialPattern calls all look up this ID when no row is passed. None or a missing row makes those helpers return before changing material-section visibility or MaterialPattern. All exported non-None IDs resolve.

Id_ShikigamiAnimation.simple: The animation sets the game loads for this summon. They cover idle movement, damage reactions, and attacks.
Id_ShikigamiAnimation.technical: TArray<FName> of animation-set IDs; all 20 export arrays have 10 slots with None padding and every non-None ID resolves in ShikigamiAnimationDataTable. Battle preload appends each referenced set's FileName array to the AnimMontage preload list; battle spawn resolves each non-None set and calls AnimInstance.SetAnimationAsset(Key[i], Montage) for its paired Key/FileName entries (skipping None pairs). Export CN_010 uses CN_010 (base), CN_010_DAMAGE and per-attack sets.

ActionControllerType.simple: Chooses how this summon acts and follows the character who called it. It also changes movement behavior and certain character-specific effects.
ActionControllerType.technical: uint8-backed EGameShikigamiActionControllerType. Exports use the matching CN_xxx enumerators, except CN_051, CN_052 and both _10 variants, which all use CN_050. Passed to AGameShikigami::CreateActionController and CreateBoneController at spawn: the switches choose controller subclasses and also set follow height, summon offset, order/placement flags and (for CN_231) effect rotation. Failure of either creator, or of CreateMaterialController, makes Setup return false. The C++ constructor default is None.

SummonCursedEnergyLevel.simple: The Cursed Energy level the character needs before calling this summon. A higher value demands a higher Cursed Energy level.
SummonCursedEnergyLevel.technical: int32; C++ constructor default 0, but all exports are explicit (1 in 19 rows, 2 in CN_020). AGameShikigami::IsSummonAvailable first compares the row value strictly greater than OwnerCharacter.StatusController.GetCursedEnergyLevelClamped(); when it is greater, summoning is rejected before the summon-cooldown check.

HitPoint.simple: How much damage this summon can take before it goes down. A higher value lets it survive more hits.
HitPoint.technical: float; C++ constructor default 0, explicitly serialized in every row (CN_010=120.0; 1.0/100.0/200.0 elsewhere). UGameShikigamiStatusController::ApplyHitPointParameters copies it to both HitPointMax and HitPoint at setup and on action-driven resets; damage later clamps and changes the current value while HitPointMax remains the row value.

DownValue.simple: How much down damage this summon takes before being knocked down. Higher values let it absorb more, and some shikigami have no down gauge.
DownValue.technical: float down/daze gauge maximum and initial value; C++ constructor default 0, explicitly serialized in every row. CN_010=150.0; 15/20 rows use -1.0. UGameShikigamiStatusController::ApplyDownValueParameters writes the row value directly to both DownValueMax and DownValue (unlike the character status setter, it does not clamp a negative value). GameBattleDamage only decrements DownValue while it is >0, so -1.0 effectively marks a shikigami with no down gauge for that path. Actions also reapply the row value to refill it.

OrderCoolTime.simple: How long the character waits before ordering this summon again. Higher values create a longer pause between orders.
OrderCoolTime.technical: float seconds; C++ constructor default 0, explicitly serialized as -1.0 in 10 rows, 0.0 in 8 rows and 0.3 in CN_010/CN_020. Setup copies it to StatusController.OrderCoolTime, and release actions re-copy the row value there. CP_030/CP_160/CP_240 order helpers start the order timer (Unknown98) from it; the timer only ticks while >0 and order checks require <=0, so non-positive values mean no order cooldown.

SummonCoolTime.simple: How long the character waits before summoning this shikigami again. Higher values create a longer wait, and some summons have no cooldown.
SummonCoolTime.technical: float seconds; C++ constructor default 0, explicitly serialized as -1.0 in 10 rows, 0.0 in 6 rows and 8.0/15.0/16.0/18.0 in four rows. Setup copies it to StatusController.SummonCoolTime; release/downed-hit paths set SummonCoolTimeLeft from it and the left value ticks down only while >0. IsSummonAvailable treats <=0 as available, and CP_030/CP_160 UI widgets display SummonCoolTimeLeft/SummonCoolTime only when the denominator is >0, so -1.0 is a no-cooldown sentinel rather than a negative duration.

bIsInstanceDeathEnabled.simple: Whether this summon immediately goes down after taking damage. Turning it on makes the next hit empty its health.
bIsInstanceDeathEnabled.technical: bool; C++ constructor default false. Exported true only for CN_051, CN_051_10 and CN_110 (3/20), false for the other 17. AGameShikigami::IsInstanceDeathEnabled returns the row flag; GameBattleDamage forces NewHitPoint to 0 whenever it is true, so the next damage application leaves the instance HP-empty regardless of its prior HitPoint.

bImmortalityEnabled.simple: Whether this summon is protected from normal defeat. When on, only the character stopping the summon defeats it.
bImmortalityEnabled.technical: bool; C++ constructor default false. Exported true for CN_040, CN_070, CN_200, CN_272 and CN_280 (5/20), false for the other 15. At the start of AGameShikigami::IsDefeated, true makes the result solely (!bRequestedActive) without consulting HP; false uses the normal path in which an empty HitPoint or an inactive request also counts as defeated.

AutoAttackDistance_Owner.simple: How far this summon can stray from the character who called it before its automatic attacks stop. A larger value allows more distance.
AutoAttackDistance_Owner.technical: float UE world-distance units; C++ constructor default 0 (all exports are positive). GetAutoAttackDistanceOwner returns the row value. Generic FGameShikigamiAttackActionBase::CanReplace rejects an auto-attack when shikigami-to-owner distance exceeds it (after the UseAutoAttackDistance check); CN_230 order/cancel logic uses the same getter, with one order path rejecting on owner distance alone. Export CN_010=1800.0.

AutoAttackDistance_Target.simple: How far this summon can be from its target to attack automatically. A larger value allows farther targets.
AutoAttackDistance_Target.technical: float UE world-distance units; C++ constructor default 0 (all exports are positive). GetAutoAttackDistanceTarget returns the row value. Generic FGameShikigamiAttackActionBase::CanReplace requires the shikigami-to-secondary-target distance to be within it when a target exists; the final comparison is !(distance > limit), so NaN counts as in range. CN_230 order/cancel checks use the same getter and refuse only when both owner and target distances are exceeded. Export CN_010=2500.0.

Id_ActionMove.simple: Which movement style this summon uses when it walks or runs. This name connects it to the game's movement settings.
Id_ActionMove.technical: FName; ActionMoveDataTable row for shikigami movement. All exports are non-None and resolve in ActionMoveDataTable. When non-None, ResolveRows looks it up in ActionMoveDataTables and caches MoveRow; a missing row makes ResolveRows return false without overwriting the previously cached row, while None is skipped. Shikigami movement code then reads cached MoveRow.

Id_ActionJump.simple: Which jumping style this summon uses. This name connects it to the game's jump settings.
Id_ActionJump.technical: FName; ActionJumpDataTable row for shikigami jumping. All exports are non-None and resolve in the ActionJumpDataTable shards; same lookup/cache pattern as Id_ActionMove over ActionJumpDataTables (cached JumpRow, +0x5D0). A missing row fails setup while leaving the old cached pointer; None is skipped. Export CN_010 uses CN_010.

Id_ActionDash.simple: Which dashing style this summon uses. This name connects it to the game's dash settings.
Id_ActionDash.technical: FName; ActionDashDataTable row for shikigami dashing. All exports are non-None and resolve in the ActionDashDataTable shards; same lookup/cache pattern over ActionDashDataTables (cached DashRow, +0x5E0). A missing row fails setup while leaving the old cached pointer; None is skipped. Export CN_010 uses CN_010.

Id_CharacterEffect.simple: Which visual settings this summon uses, including aura colors and effect size. Leaving it empty uses the standard values.
Id_CharacterEffect.technical: FName; None in 18/20 exports, otherwise CN_110 or CN_231. Resolved by Shikigami_FindRow over CharacterEffectDataTables (+0x4D0) during ResolveRows and cached as EffectRow; None leaves it null. The cached row supplies shikigami effect tuning: GetMapGroundEffectScale falls back to (1,1,1) without it and CN_110's aura reads BuffDebuffEffectScale and aura colors. This field does NOT drive battle preload: BattleAssets_CharacterEffects appends FileName_BP from the Character row's own Id_CharacterEffect instead.

Id_CharacterSound.simple: Which sound settings this summon uses, including its footstep sounds. Leaving it empty leaves footstep sounds at their default.
Id_CharacterSound.technical: FName; None in 17/20 exports, otherwise CN_020, CN_081 or CN_111. Resolved via Shikigami_FindCharacterSoundRow (retail 0x14147E710) over CharacterSoundDataTables (+0x510) with bCheckNone=true and cached as SoundRow. The cached row's FootstepType is returned by AGameShikigami::GetFootstepType, which yields 0 when no row resolved; this field is not the character-variation sound ID used by the battle asset collector.

Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_DefaultAction.simple: Which voice lines this summon uses for general actions like starting, dashing, or jumping. Choosing a group allows battle voices to play.
Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_DefaultAction.technical: FName (row +0x7C); None in 18/20 exports, otherwise CN_040_DEFAULTACTION or CN_080_DEFAULTACTION. PlayVoice case 1 resolves it in ShikigamiVoiceGroupDataTables. Value directly indexes ShikigamiVoiceGroup.Id_VoiceGroup with no bounds check; that FName is then looked up in VoiceGroupDataTables and one of its non-None Id_Voice entries is chosen randomly for playback, gated by bActionVoiceEnabled and bVoiceGroupPlaybackEnabled. Any non-None voice-group field causes SetBattleVoiceEnabled to set the latter flag.

Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Attack.simple: Which voice lines this summon uses when attacking. Different attacks pick from the group, and choosing one allows battle voices to play.
Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Attack.technical: FName (row +0x84); None in 17/20 exports, otherwise CN_040_ATTACK, CN_070_ATTACK or CN_080_ATTACK. PlayVoice case 3 requires Value>0 and indexes ShikigamiVoiceGroup.Id_VoiceGroup[Value-1] without a bounds check; the selected FName is then resolved in VoiceGroupDataTables for random cue selection.

Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Damage.simple: Which voice lines this summon uses when reacting to damage. Different hits pick from the group, and choosing one allows battle voices to play.
Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Damage.technical: FName (row +0x8C); None in 18/20 exports, otherwise CN_040_DAMAGE or CN_080_DAMAGE. PlayVoice case 6 requires Value>0 and indexes Id_VoiceGroup[Value-1] without a bounds check before the VoiceGroupDataTables lookup and random cue selection.

Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Down.simple: Which voice lines this summon uses when knocked down. Different down events pick from the group, and choosing one allows battle voices to play.
Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Down.technical: FName (row +0x94); None in 19/20 exports, otherwise CN_080_DOWN. PlayVoice case 8 indexes Id_VoiceGroup[Value] directly with no bounds check before the VoiceGroupDataTables lookup and random cue selection; exported arrays include None holes, so event values matter.

Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Unique.simple: Which voice lines this summon uses during special actions. Different actions pick from the group, and choosing one allows battle voices to play.
Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Unique.technical: FName (row +0x9C); None in 17/20 exports, otherwise CN_040_UNIQUE, CN_080_UNIQUE or CN_200_UNIQUE. PlayVoice case 10 indexes Id_VoiceGroup[Value] directly with no bounds check before the VoiceGroupDataTables lookup and random cue selection.

Id_ShikigamiUnique.simple: Which special-move settings this summon uses. The choices are read in order, and empty choices leave gaps.
Id_ShikigamiUnique.technical: TArray<FName>; every export array has 8 slots and all non-None IDs resolve in ShikigamiUniqueDataTable. ResolveRows clears the cache, then appends one ShikigamiUniqueDataTables result per slot; None or missing IDs become nullptr entries rather than being skipped. Consumers call GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(ValueIndex, RowIndex) through the actor interface with the array position as RowIndex, using UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] with no bounds or null checks. Export CN_010 has base and per-attack entries followed by None padding.

FootIKLimit.simple: For one summon type, this controls how far its hands and feet reach while settling onto surfaces. Larger values allow longer reach.
FootIKLimit.technical: TArray<double>; C++ constructor default empty, but all 20 export arrays have 4 doubles. CreateBoneController copies the array into a local and passes it to InitBoneController(ActionControllerType, &Limits). The shikigami UCN_020_BoneController uses element [0] for all four limb limits (CN_020 exports 100.0 there, 0.0 elsewhere; all other shikigami rows are all zero). The same TArray<double> convention is used by character bone controllers where, for example, CN_140 uses [0] for legs and [1] for arms; that [1] behavior should not be attributed to the shikigami controller. In the reconstructed row header this member is EditAnywhere only, without BlueprintReadWrite.

notes: ShikigamiDataTables is manager slot +0x6C0; the name is registered at GameDataTableManager.cpp:410 and resolved at line 238. CharacterShikigamiDataTable (+0x4F0) is the per-character selection table that points here. Shared finders scan manager table arrays in registration order and return the first match; the current build registers one ShikigamiDataTable.

ResolveRows first stores ShikigamiRow, then treats linked rows differently: non-None Id_ActionMove/Jump/Dash must resolve or it returns false without overwriting the cached Move/Jump/Dash row, while None is skipped. Id_ShikigamiUnique appends one cache entry per slot, including nullptr for None/missing. CharacterEffect and CharacterSound use None-rejecting finders and tolerate None by leaving their cached pointer null. Setup/battle-spawn/capture callers generally ignore Setup's false result, so a failed linked lookup can leave a partially initialized actor.

All 20 exported rows explicitly serialize all 26 fields and share the same schema; there are no localization variants or numbered shards for this table. C++ constructor defaults (empty FNames/TArrays, None enum, zeros and false) are reconstruction fallback values, not omitted shipped cells. Exported non-None IDs resolve in their respective linked-table exports/shards.

Negative/non-positive cooldown values are meaningful sentinels: OrderCoolTime is -1.0 in 10 rows and 0.0 in 8, while SummonCoolTime is -1.0 in 10 rows and 0.0 in 6. Timers only tick and gates only block while the active timer is >0, and UI ratios guard a positive denominator, so these behave as no cooldown. DownValue=-1.0 (15 rows) similarly means no usable down gauge in the damage path.

Voice-group indexing conventions are per-event and unchecked: DefaultAction/Down/Unique use Value directly, Attack/Damage require Value>0 and use Value-1. The indexed FName selects a row from ShikigamiVoiceGroupDataTable, whose Id_Voice array is then randomly sampled through VoiceGroupDataTables and VoiceDataTables.

Exported field names, native types and values are retail-data evidence; runtime mechanics described here come from the current reconstructed C++ (whose comments cite retail RVAs). No Blueprint-only or unobserved retail behavior is asserted.

usages.detail: Battle preload joins CharacterShikigami -> Shikigami rows and collects FileName_BP plus montage filenames from each referenced ShikigamiAnimation row.
Battle spawn resolves the row through the CharacterShikigami join, obtains its Blueprint loader class, calls SpawnShikigami, and registers Key/FileName montage pairs on the spawned anim instance.

ResolveRows caches ActionMove/Jump/Dash, ShikigamiUnique, CharacterEffect and CharacterSound rows; missing non-None movement rows fail setup while None entries are skipped or become null cache entries as appropriate.
Setup seeds the status controller from HitPoint, DownValue, SummonCoolTime and OrderCoolTime before creating action, bone and material controllers.
Spawn creates the action and bone controllers from ActionControllerType and FootIKLimit; the enum switch also configures movement/order flags and the CN_231 effect rotation.

Generic attack replacement checks shikigami-owner and shikigami-target distances against AutoAttackDistance_Owner/_Target; CN_230 action/order logic reuses both getters with different rejection combinations.
Damage application asks IsInstanceDeathEnabled and forces HP to zero for flagged summons; positive DownValue is decremented and can trigger the down action.
PlayVoice resolves the five voice-group IDs into ShikigamiVoiceGroup rows, indexes their Id_VoiceGroup arrays per event, then resolves a VoiceGroup row and randomly selects a voice.
Cached EffectRow from Id_CharacterEffect supplies GetMapGroundEffectScale; CN_110's active-set aura also reads that cached row's scale and colors.
Cached SoundRow from Id_CharacterSound supplies GetFootstepType, returning 0 when no row was resolved.
Sequencer support-character binding finds an owned shikigami by comparing its cached ShikigamiRow->Id with the binding character ID.
Sequencer actor rebinding checks cached Row->Id against the model name and, on mismatch, re-resolves the ShikigamiDataTable row with Setup(bRowsOnly=true).
Character-specific battle UI selects icons from cached ShikigamiRow->Id and displays the summon-cooldown ratio copied into the status controller.
